title: How Matt Pocock runs an AI coding workflow: grill, PRD, Kanban issues, AFK agents, deep modules
summary: A 2-hour workshop where Matt applies old-school software engineering fundamentals to coding agents. He covers the smart/dumb zone, aligning with a "grill me" session, a PRD as destination, vertical-slice Kanban issues, AFK Ralph loops with TDD, and deepening modules so code bases are testable.

principles.text: LLMs get dumber as context grows, so size tasks to stay in the smart zone (~100K tokens).
principles.quote: it doesn't matter whether you're using 1 million uh context window or 200K, it's always going to be about this. It starts to just get dumber.

principles.text: Prefer clearing context to compacting so every session starts from the same known state.
principles.quote: I much prefer my AI to behave like uh the guy from Memento because this state is always the same.

principles.text: Reach a shared design concept with the agent through a relentless grilling session, not an eager plan.
principles.quote: I didn't need a plan, I needed to be on the same wavelength as the AI, as my agent.

principles.text: Reject specs-to-code: keep a handle on the code, because the code is the battleground.
principles.quote: You need to keep a handle on the code. You need to understand what's in it. You need to shape it because the code is your battleground.

principles.text: Split work into vertical slices (tracer bullets), not horizontal layers, so the agent gets feedback early.
principles.quote: You don't get feedback on your work until you've really started or completed phase three.

principles.text: Build code bases from deep modules with small interfaces; design the interface, delegate the implementation.
principles.quote: Modules that have a little interface on there that expose a small, simple interface that have a lot of functionality inside them.
